title: A Phone Geofence Now Clocks Dad's Delivery Shifts | vitalii.no
description:
My dad's delivery shifts always start at a fixed 02:15, but what each one actually paid him was never written down anywhere. Tracking tariffs, after-hours rates and unpaid breaks by hand meant he couldn't check a month's total without redoing all the math from memory, weeks after the fact.

An OwnTracks geofence around the depot now posts a transition event the moment his phone leaves, straight to a new /work-event route on a Cloudflare Worker. The worker attributes the event to the right work day and writes it into a new Postgres work_shifts table, locked down with row-level security so only the worker's own service key can reach it. Pure functions turn the raw timestamps into worked minutes, split pay before and after 06:00 at each tariff's rate, and subtract any unpaid break over 330 minutes. A new monthly report expands every day into its own row with a reason attached, a kiosk screen shows a live badge for today and the month, and a parent can open a full-screen report to page between months or correct a day's end time by hand — each manual edit flagged so a later geofence reading never overwrites it.

Shift pay now gets computed and recorded the moment the phone leaves the depot, instead of being reconstructed from memory weeks later. A parent can open any month on the kiosk itself and see exactly which days counted, which didn't, and why.
